title: Ops workbench: Patchlet orchestration for first-line support
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Enable first-line support to safely execute small, tested remediation units ("patchlets") from a guided ops workbench. Patchlets are compact, idempotent actions derived from runbook steps (e.g., restart a pooled worker, flush a KV prefix, temporarily scale a pod). The goal is to reduce mean time to resolution for common incidents while preserving auditability, RBAC controls, and dry-run validation.
background: Oncall and support currently rely on long narrative runbooks or ad-hoc scripts. That increases cognitive load, error rates, and time-to-fix. This work converts high-frequency runbook actions into discrete patchlets that can be composed, validated, and executed via an internal web workbench and a safe server-side executor.
acceptance_criteria: Workbench UI: list + search of approved patchlets with parameterized inputs and in-context help
Executor: server-side sandboxed execution with dry-run option and automatic idempotency checks
Safety: RBAC gating + approval flow for high-risk patchlets, circuit breaker for repeated failures
Observability: per-execution audit log, structured telemetry (success/failure, latency, tokens affected), and dashboard in Console
Regression plan: feature flag + canary rollout to internal support team before org-wide enablement
technical_notes: Patchlet DSL: small YAML schema (name, description, params, prechecks, execute, rollback) to be stored in repo and surfaced in console

Executor architecture: run requests through ops-orchestrator service which validates, records audit event, and enqueues to a constrained worker pool with plugin-based adapters (k8s, redis, runtime-admin)
Idempotency: patchlets must declare resource keys and a deterministic guard to avoid repeated side effects
Dry-run: executor executes prechecks and simulates changes without state mutation; uses a separate dry-run path for external systems where available
Security: requests require scoped service token tied to user session; all executions require KMS-wrapped credentials for downstream infra where applicable
Telemetry: emit span and metric per patchlet execution, include inputs (redacted) and result codes for SLO monitoring
tasks: Spike: prototype YAML patchlet schema and author 5 canonical patchlets (restart-worker, flush-prefix, rotate-log, scale-pool, toggle-feature)
Backend: implement ops-orchestrator endpoints, dry-run mode, enqueueing, worker adapters
Frontend: workbench UI to browse, parameterize, preview, and invoke patchlets
Security: integrate with RBAC, approval workflow, and KMS credential access
Observability: dashboard card + execution table and alert rules for failure rate > 5%
Tests: unit and e2e, simulated dry-run against staging infra, chaos test to verify circuit breaker
Docs: editorial runbook -> patchlet migration guide and support runbook in Confluence
Rollout: feature flag, pilot with support team, expand after two weeks and success metrics met

notes_on_tradeoffs: Centralized executor vs local ad-hoc scripts: chose centralized to enforce audit and RBAC at the cost of added latency
DSL complexity: keep DSL minimal to reduce review surface; advanced workflows should remain in authored runbooks
Prechecks vs full simulation: for third-party systems we rely on existing dry-run endpoints where available rather than full simulation
rollout_plan: Pilot group: internal support (10 users) for 2 weeks
Collect metrics: time-to-resolution for targeted incidents, execution failure rate, manual override frequency
Gradual ramp: 25% org -> 50% -> 100% following success criteria and security signoff
